name: Slavoj Žižek
shortBio: Slovenian philosopher, cultural theorist, and co-founder of the Ljubljana School of Psychoanalysis who synthesizes Hegelian dialectics, Marxian political economy, and Lacanian psychoanalysis to expose how unconscious fantasy and enjoyment sustain contemporary ideology.
centralQuestion: If contemporary subjects already maintain a cynical, ironic distance toward official power, how does ideology nonetheless grip our unconscious enjoyment and structure social reality itself?

keyWorks.title: The Sublime Object of Ideology
keyWorks.description: Landmark English-language debut reconceiving ideology not as naive false consciousness, but as an unconscious Lacanian social fantasy anchored by a sublime object (objet petit a).

keyWorks.title: Tarrying with the Negative: Kant, Hegel, and the Critique of Ideology
keyWorks.description: Reclaims the Cartesian cogito and German Idealist negativity through Lacan, analyzing nationalist enjoyment ('theft of enjoyment') in post-communist Eastern Europe.

keyWorks.title: The Parallax View
keyWorks.description: Systematic philosophical magnum opus articulating dialectical materialism through the 'parallax gap'—the irreducible ontological shift between two incompatible perspectives with no neutral common ground.

keyWorks.title: Less Than Nothing: Hegel and the Shadow of Dialectical Materialism
keyWorks.description: Monumental reinterpretation of G.W.F. Hegel via Jacques Lacan, arguing that reality itself is ontologically incomplete ('less than nothing') and constituted by antagonism.
